findings.title: include_website_name is missing the '?' suffix required by the serializer convention
findings.body: The serializer uses the `include_#{attr}?` naming convention everywhere else (e.g. `include_card_image_badge_id?`, `include_card_image_badge?`, `include_user_fields?`). The newly added guard method is named `include_website_name` without the trailing `?`, so ActiveModel::Serializer will never find/call it to decide inclusion. As a result the `website_name` attribute is always serialized regardless of whether `website` is present, defeating the intended `website.present?` guard and potentially emitting `website_name: null` when there is no website.

findings.title: website_name bypasses the untrusted_attributes privacy restriction applied to website
findings.body: `website` is listed under `untrusted_attributes`, which hides it from anonymous users when the owning user is TL0 (via `scope.restrict_user_fields?`), presumably to prevent spam-link exposure. The new `website_name` attribute computes its value directly from `object.user_profile.website` and is only declared in the plain `attributes` list (with the broken `include_website_name` guard, see other finding), completely bypassing the untrusted-attribute restriction. This means a TL0 user's website host/path is still leaked to anonymous viewers via `website_name` even though `website` itself is correctly suppressed, undermining the existing privacy/anti-spam protection.

findings.title: Test for untrusted attributes was not updated to cover the new website_name attribute
findings.body: The `untrusted_attributes` array used in the 'with a TL0 user seen as anonymous' context still only lists `%i{bio_raw bio_cooked bio_excerpt location website profile_background card_background}` and was not updated to include `:website_name`. Since `website_name` is derived from the same `website` data that this test is meant to protect, the missing entry means the test suite would not catch the regression where `website_name` leaks website information for TL0 users viewed anonymously (see related serializer finding).
